title: The last stand of Taffy 3
photoNote: USS Gambier Bay and her escorts making smoke during the Battle off Samar, 25 October 1944. U.S. Navy photo, public domain.
body:
Six small escort carriers and seven little warships looked to the horizon at dawn and saw the biggest battleship in the world coming for them.

25 October 1944. Off the island of Samar, an American group called Taffy 3 was there to fly air support for the troops on Leyte, not to fight battleships. Then Admiral Takeo Kurita's Center Force appeared: four battleships, including the giant Yamato, six heavy cruisers, two light cruisers, and eleven destroyers.

Rear Admiral Clifton Sprague ordered smoke, turned away, and called for help. His three destroyers and four destroyer escorts turned the other way and charged the battleships, firing torpedoes from close range. Planes from the little carriers attacked again and again.

It cost Taffy 3 two carriers, two destroyers, and a destroyer escort. Then, at 9:20, Kurita ordered his fleet north and broke off the battle. That same morning, the first organized kamikaze attacks hit the escort carriers, and one sank St. Lo.

#OnThisDay #WW2 #LeyteGulf
